$comment: Contract for workspace/harnesses/harness_<module>.json, written by scripts/generate_harness.py (and, for `--api`, completed by scripts/api_harness.py with `api_harness`, `api_cases` and `api_skipped`). Kept up to date by `--record-repair` and harness_reach.py exempt. Read by pipeline_make.py (recipes), run_eacsl_fuzz.py, module_map.py (unit, scope), harness_reach.py (reach_exempt), seed_harvest.py write (api_cases) and the WP side. Fields a consumer reads are typed; the producer may add more.

slot.$comment: Input bytes feeding one argument: `call` is the position of the call in the case (initializer calls of `inits` come after the case's `calls`), `param` its argument index, `size` the bytes read (null: the scalar's size is unknown). The field kinds fill one field of a struct argument that holds pointers, never a pointer itself: `field` a scalar or pointer-free field at byte `off`, `field_bytes` the storage of the (pointer, length) pair at `off`, `field_len` that pair's length, clamped to `max` bytes.

rest.$comment: The argument that takes the rest of the input, after the slots; `off`: the byte offset of the (pointer, length) field pair of a struct argument that takes it.

init.$comment: An initializer the case calls first on a struct object of call `for.call`, argument `for.param`; `call` numbers its slots.

entry.$comment: the DAG key of the API entry point the case calls

notes.$comment: arguments the generator zeroed instead of reading from the input, and why
arguments the generator zeroed instead of reading from the input, and why

lifecycle_case.$comment: A synthesized call sequence on one opaque handle (api_harness.lifecycle_case): `calls` are its constructor (call 0, whose arguments are the slots; it never takes the rest of the input, so `rest` is null: an unsized input string is a `bytes` slot of api_harness.STRING_SLOT_BYTES, its last byte forced to 0) and destructor; up to `max_calls` calls of `methods`, each picked by one input byte, run on the handle in between, their arguments read from the input in the loop.

notes.$comment: arguments the generator zeroed instead of reading from the input, and why

custom_case.$comment: A hand-written case (generate_harness.py --api --dispatch-case), after the generated ones: its statements are `dispatch_cases[selector]`. No calls and no slots: the seed writers make nothing for it.

vararg.$comment: One object a variadic case passes after the format: `type` is its type at the call site (`struct minmea_float`, `char[80]`), `pass` how it is passed: `addr` (`&object`) or `array` (the array by name). The case declares it with exactly that type, zeroed; no input byte goes into it.

variadic_case.$comment: One call of a variadic API function as a call site of the target's own programs makes it (api_harness.variadic_case, from workspace/reports/variadic_calls.json): `format` is that call site's string literal (its bytes as latin-1 text), passed as parameter `format_param` (the last fixed one) and never read from the input; `varargs` are the objects passed after it. `slots` and `rest` cover the other fixed parameters, as in a single case. A function has one such case per distinct (format, varargs), all with the same `entry`.

entry.$comment: the DAG key of the API entry point the case calls

notes.$comment: arguments the generator zeroed instead of reading from the input, and why

unit.$comment: the link unit (DAG module) this harness module belongs to; null without link units

scope_files.$comment: files whose functions a sub-module answers for at the reach gate (generate_harness.py --scope-file, kept on regeneration); empty means `sources`

extra_includes_first.$comment: the `extra_includes` the prelude resolution moved before `header`, because the header needs what they define; absent when none was moved

dispatch_selector.$comment: how a dispatch harness's first input bytes select its case (generate_harness.py): `identity`, the first byte is the case index and a byte at or above `dispatch_case_count` runs no case; `identity16`, for more than 256 cases, the same with the first two bytes, little-endian. Absent on a dispatch harness generated before the field existed, which selects with the first byte modulo `dispatch_case_count`; every decoder (run_eacsl_fuzz.py, harness_reach.py) reads it that way.

api_skipped.$comment: API entry points (DAG keys) the generator could not call, with the reason. A variadic function is here only when none of its call sites made a case

api_helpers.$comment: Functions from outside the module's scope (another cluster of the unit) the cases call only to set up or release a struct object: its initializer and destructor (api_harness.case_helpers). harness_reach.check_module counts none of them as a root of the module. Absent on an older sidecar.

api_headers.$comment: Where the headers of an --api harness came from (api_harness.capture_headers): `given` (--header), `none` (--header none), `capture` (no --header: the build capture's public headers the module's link unit includes, plus the internal headers declaring an entry point no public header declares, with the names), `not_found` (no --header and the capture gave none; `why` says why), or `capture_failed` (none of the capture's headers compiled in the harness: it includes none, as without a capture). An automatic choice degrades in steps (all chosen headers, then the public ones alone, then none) and never fails the module for its own headers; `fallbacks` lists each abandoned step, the headers it dropped and the first compile errors. `public` and `internal` list what the final harness includes. Paths are tree-relative. Absent on an older sidecar.

api_variadic_dropped.$comment: Call sites of a variadic entry point that made no case (over a cap, a type the harness cannot declare, a case the compiler refused), with the reason. Absent when there is none.

target_fuzzer.$comment: Set on a target fuzz module (generate_harness.py --target-fuzzer): the harness calls the target's own LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput, renamed to __framac_target_embedded_LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput; `initialize` is true when the fuzzer also defines LLVMFuzzerInitialize (renamed and called once by the harness). Absent on every other module.
